svg.title: Hungary wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Place nine selected study areas around northeastern hills, western volcanic landscapes, southern districts and the central plain. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Tokaj. Northeastern Hungary at the Zemplén foothills; the Hungarian region is more extensive than this locator. 2: Eger. Northern Hungary southwest of Tokaj. 3: Mátra. Northern Hungary around the Mátra foothills, west of Eger. 4: Sopron. Far western Hungary near Austria and Lake Neusiedl/Fertő. 5: Badacsony (Balaton). On the northern shore of Lake Balaton. 6: Somló. A distinct volcanic hill northwest of Lake Balaton. 7: Szekszárd. Southern Hungary west of the Danube, north and east of Villány. 8: Villány. Far southern Hungary near Croatia. 9: Kunság. The broad central plain between the Danube and Tisza; one locator cannot show its full extent.

g.text: Dots: representative places · outlines: geography, not appellation boundaries

text.tspan: Discover volcanic hills, lake shores and the
central plain through the stories of wine.
